title: Fire component card
description: The judgement about one component that cannot be generated from the source: when to use it, when not to, and what it is called elsewhere. One file per component, contract/cards/<component id>.json. Every field is required; a list with nothing to say is [].

id.description: The component id in contract/catalog.json, equal to the file name without .json.

job.description: One sentence, starting with a verb a user would say: what the component lets someone do.

purpose.description: What it is and how it behaves, in plain prose. At most 500 characters.

useWhen.description: Situations that call for it, each one sentence.

avoidWhen.description: Situations that look like a fit and are not, with what to use instead.

instead.description: A component id, or a short instruction when no component fits.

aka.description: Other names people and other design systems use for it (search terms).

data.description: The shape of data it shows or collects.

states.description: Conditions it can be in, and how markup expresses each.

how.description: The attribute, class or call that sets it, written as it appears in markup.

variants.description: Attribute values that change the look or role. attribute and value must be ones catalog.json lists for the component.

value.description: The attribute value; an empty string for an attribute that is set with no value (data-icon-only).

parts.description: The classes that make up the component, each with its role. Every class must belong to the component in catalog.json.

related.description: Ids of components often used with it or mistaken for it.

example.description: The docs section whose specimen shows it: docs/<page>.html#<section id>. The build checks it exists.

provenance.description: Repository paths the card was written from (docs pages, component CSS, module headers).

since.description: The Fire version that introduced the component.
